ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and signatories against the UN Security Council consolidated list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, French national asset-freeze list (Direction générale du Trésor), and OFAC SDN list to the extent USD-denominated payment rails are used. Enhanced due diligence applies to any PEP, direct or indirect government role, or diplomatic/residency status. Screening must be performed prior to filing and re-run at least annually; all records must be retained for a minimum of five years under the Sapin II regime.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet des formalités des entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), in conjunction with the Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS) maintained by INPI and the local Greffe du tribunal de commerce
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name may include foreign-language words, but the articles of association and all French statutory filings must display a Latin-script denomination capable of French transliteration. Non-Latin script names are not recordable; accents must be preserved. The memorandum must state the registered French company name for service of process and official publications.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate a standalone name-reservation system. Upon a formal rejection by the Greffe du tribunal de commerce, the applicant must file a 'réclamation' within 15 days through the Guichet des formalités des entreprises with a revised name. If the rejection persists, a written request for review may be submitted to the presiding judge of the commercial court (juge commissaire), who may direct the registrar to proceed. Any civil action against a conflicting name is available only after incorporation is completed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permitted: an SAS may use a domiciliation agent or business incubator address under Article L.123-11-1 of the French Commercial Code, provided the address is physically located in France and staffed to receive official legal process. A pure mailbox or unstaffed virtual address without a French reception agent is not accepted by the RCS for a commercial manufacturing/retail entity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk: approximately 8–10% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection per year for a cashless, distance-selling manufacturer of tabletop RPG dice. The probability rises to 15–20% if the registered office is an unapproved virtual address or if any UBO is classified as a PEP.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code of Commerce, articles L. 227-1 to L. 227-36 governing simplified joint-stock companies (Sociétés par actions simplifiées)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registry Office (Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce) and INSEE
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital of 1 euro; no escrow account required
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board of Directors of the proposed Société par Actions Simplifiée, duly convened and unanimously resolved: 1. To approve incorporation under French law pursuant to the Code of Commerce. 2. To subscribe to the initial share capital of one euro by the incorporator(s). 3. To adopt the registered office at the designated address in France. 4. To appoint [Director Name] as Président and [Director Name] as gérant. 5. To authorize deposit of the share capital and filing of the Articles of Association, Certificate of Incorporation, and supporting documents with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce. 6. To empower the officers to complete all statutory formalities and obtain the Kbis extract. This resolution complies fully with articles L. 227-1 et seq. of the Code of Commerce.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and signing of corporate statutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and finalize the Articles of Association specifying company name, registered office, share capital, corporate object, and directors. All shareholders sign the documents. Deposit the minimum 1 euro share capital into a bank account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Provide any missing documents or make amendments within 8 days to prevent rejection

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of incorporation documents with the registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via guichet-entreprises.fr or infogreffe.fr
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Certificate of Incorporation, signed Articles of Association, proof of capital deposit, and director identification documents to the registry. Pay the filing fee and request registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Submit additional information or corrected documents within 15 days if the application is queried

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication and issuance of Kbis extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish the incorporation notice in the legal gazette if required. Obtain the official Kbis extract confirming registration and extract the company details.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Follow up directly with the greffe for any delays or to request corrections

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Relevant prefecture or chamber of commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File any required local declarations or permits for the commercial premises and business operations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Address any requested additional documents promptly to expedite approval

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No specific industrial licensing board required for artisanal tabletop gaming activities
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating license mandated for small-scale handmade production

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for resin storage areas; structural safety inspections for workshop premises; workplace safety clearance from the Labour Inspectorate

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Generale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP), French Ministry of Economy and Finance, acting with the Direction Generale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) for export controls; primary portal is impots.gouv.fr (Professional Space); company registration is administered via the INPI Guichet Unique at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The French SAS is constituted through the INPI Guichet Unique (08 February 2023 single-window regime). The president/legal representative files the digital registration package comprising the articles of association (statuts), proof of registered office, identity and residential address of the president, and, where relevant, the foreign parent company's certificate of incorporation and power of attorney. INSEE automatically allocates the 9-digit SIREN and the subsidiary SIRET code; DGFIP enters the company in the French VAT register (assujetti a la TVA) from the first taxable transaction and, where intra-Community transactions or distance sales are made, assigns the statutory French VAT identification (Intra-Community VAT ID, e.g., FR47XXXXX). A definitive NIF/SIREN confirmation is issued as an extrait d'immatriculation au registre national des entreprises through the Guichet Unique dashboard. Non-EU foreign sellers without a French fixed establishment use the specific non-established procedure (form 1536-SDF) through the same portal or the nearest DGFIP non-resident section; processing time is generally 5 to 15 business days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in France. The default regime is corporate income tax (impot sur les societes, IS) levied at 25%, with the reduced IS rate of 15% on the first EUR 42,500 of annual profit for SMEs with turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million. Available statutory elections: (i) option for personal income tax (option IR) under Article 239 bis AA CGI, available to qualifying SMEs for five fiscal years and tacitly renewable (with mandatory dividend treatment adjustments and restrictions on depreciation of the initial franchise value); (ii) VAT fiscal unity election (groupe TVA) under Article 256 C bis CGI for closely-linked French entities; (iii) French tax consolidation (integration fiscale) under Article 223 A CGI, applicable to a 95%-owned group of French subsidiaries, on a five-year elective basis; and (iv) automatic hybrid-mismatch qualification under EU ATAD 2 implemented by Article 212 bis A CGI, which is not elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: TVA (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutee / French VAT implementing Council Directive 2006/112/EC)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Domestic: no net turnover threshold — a French SAS is subject to VAT from the first taxable supply; nevertheless, the small-enterprise exemption (franchise en base de TVA) under Article 293 B CGI applies to goods/activities suppliers with turnover below EUR 85,000 (2025), with an option for taxation. Intra-EU distance sales of goods by a French SAS are within the EUR 10,000 EU-wide distance-selling threshold (Article 293 B CGI); above this threshold French VAT must be declared and paid via the OSS (One-Stop-Shop) regime. Non-EU suppliers selling into France have no minimum threshold: VAT registration is mandatory from the first sale.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France applies the EU ViDA-aligned e-invoicing reform (Ordonnance 2021-1190, Decret 2022-1299 as amended). B2B domestic transactions must be issued and received as structured electronic invoices (Factur-X, UBL or CII) transmitted through the national Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) or a registered Platforme de Dematerialisation Partenaire (PDP). Deadlines: from 1 September 2026 all VAT-registered entities must be able to receive e-invoices, while grandes entreprises and ETIs must issue them; from 1 September 2027 SMEs and micro-enterprises must issue them. E-reporting to DGFIP covers B2C transactions and cross-border B2B data. Communication is exclusively by API between the issuer's software/partner platform and the PPF/PDP; transmission must occur within one business day. France does not apply real-time fiscal pre-clearance or digital stamping; a qualified electronic signature or seal is optional. Non-compliance triggers Article 1737 CGI invoicing fines (EUR 15 per offence, capped at EUR 15,000 per entity, increased to proportional penalties up to 50% of concealed amounts in bad faith), together with ordinary documentary controls and potential tax audit adjustments.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods, including hand-cast epoxy-resin polyhedral dice and tabletop gaming accessories, are taxable at 0% under Article 262-1-1° CGI provided: (i) the goods are physically exported outside the customs territory of the European Union; (ii) transport commences within 90 days of the transfer of power over the goods; (iii) the goods demonstrably arrive outside the EU; and (iv) the complete documentary package proving movement is retained by the SAS. Services directly related to exported goods follow the B2B destination principle (Article 259 A CGI) and are zero-rated where the business customer is established outside France. Sales funded via Kickstarter/Stripe/PayPal qualify as exports when the goods are dispatched from France to a non-EU address and the transport receipt is reproducible; volume discounts, promotion packaging and freight packing do not disqualify zero-rating provided sale and export are sequential and evidenced.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFIP applies strict documentary audit to zero-rated export transactions. If the export evidence is incomplete, shipment is disproved, or goods return to the EU, the 20% VAT is clawed back on the gross invoice value, together with late interest (interet de retard, approximately 0.4% per month) and penalties under Article 1729 CGI: 40% for deliberate misstatement and 80% for abuse or manoeuvres frauduleuses; additional fines apply under Article 1737 CGI; intentional fraud triggers Article 1741 CGI with fines up to EUR 75,000 and imprisonment of five years for the SAS president. Foreign-currency export proceeds must be received and repatriated to the SAS's French bank account within 180 days of the invoice due date; unjustified deferral risks recharacterisation under the French foreign-exchange documentation regime, additional assessments, and denial of the zero-rating refund. A request for refund of the VAT credit balance (remboursement de credit de TVA) is filed via form 3517-SIE with the local Service des Impots des Entreprises; for annual refund claims below EUR 600 a simplified declaration suffices, while higher claims require full e-audit validation and the maintained export evidence bunch is at all times the primary safeguard against clawback.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), acting as the National Central Bank and as the operator of the French balance-of-payments and external financial accounts reporting framework, in coordination with the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) and the French Treasury (Direction Générale du Trésor) within the Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté industrielle et numérique.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is part of the eurozone and applies the euro as its legal tender. Capital account and current account operations are fully liberalized under EU Treaty provisions, particularly Articles 63–66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. Inbound and outbound foreign exchange transactions in any freely convertible currency are not subject to exchange controls or licensing. Profit remittance by an SAS to non-resident shareholders is generally unrestricted if the entity is in good standing, corporate tax returns are filed, and any applicable treaty documentation is maintained. For non-EU investors, the only practical hurdles are anti-money-laundering verification by the receiving bank, French balance-of-payments statistical reporting for specific cross-border transactions, and, where the investor is resident in a high-risk jurisdiction, enhanced due-diligence reviews. No withholding tax is applied on dividends to residents of France or the EEA under French domestic law, and non-EEA residents may benefit from tax-treaty rates provided they submit the required certificate of residence. There are no currency convertibility restrictions affecting the distribution of attributable profits.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export proceeds surrender requirement under French law. Exporters are permitted to receive and retain proceeds in foreign currency in French-licensed bank accounts, and there is no mandatory conversion ratio or deadline for converting export receipts into euros. However, export proceeds must be declared to the Banque de France in the monthly balance-of-payments reporting if the individual transaction or aggregated flows exceed the stated thresholds, and the underlying commercial invoice and customs export declaration (including the EX1 form or the relevant Single Administrative Document) must be retained as audit evidence. For all euro-area trade settlements, SEPA Credit Transfers are used; for non-euro-area counterparties, the exporter may freely receive SWIFT MT103 payments in EUR or any convertible currency.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech EMI viability is Medium under the French PSD2 framework. Electronic Money Institutions and Payment Institutions authorized in their European Economic Area home state may passport into France and accept a French SAS as a payment-service user, but they cannot provide an equivalent of a full licensed French commercial bank account. TransferWise/Borderless and similar EEA-authorized EMIs can be used for fast cross-border currency conversion and isolation of payment flows, yet they do not satisfy all statutory escrow or share capital blocking requirements and are generally treated as supplemental payment rails rather than as a substitute for a tier-1 French bank. Non-EEA offshore digital EMIs without a valid EEA license or a French ACPR passport are legally unusable for the French SAS treasury operation and create a severe AML/regulatory risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French banks generally require at least one initial interview with the legal representative and each beneficial owner of the SAS. Physical presence is no longer an absolute rule: banks that have implemented compliant video-KYC and digital onboarding accept a dual videoconference interview combined with electronic signature and secure transmission of identity documents. For a simple low-risk SAS engaged in tabletop gaming accessories with paper-company characteristics, remote opening is acceptable if the director is physically resident in a recognized jurisdiction and appoints a local registered operational address. Non-resident directors should expect a stricter documentary defense: certified/notarized passports, original or certified company formation documents, apostilled corporate resolutions for director’s authority, and a bank-specific questionnaire on source of funds and commercial rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of a residential address or virtual office as the sole registered office of the SAS.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a tenancy agreement or commercial lease in the SAS name, an electricity/telecom invoice dated within the last three months, and, if applicable, the signed domiciliation agreement with a licensed French domiciliation company (e.g., an authorised corporate service provider). If remote manufacturing is used, add a detailed explanation of subcontracted production and the physical warehouse where the epoxy resin dice are assembled and dispatched.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound share capital contributions from a non-resident shareholder are executed by a SWIFT MT103 or an international wire transfer from the contributor’s bank to the French SAS’s euro-denominated IBAN (FR76 prefix for a bank domiciled in France). The message must clearly state the purpose as 'Share Capital Contribution – Société par Actions Simplifiée [legal name]', and the contributor must include the French banking statistical classification code for 'apports en capital / capital social' used in Banque de France balance-of-payments reporting. If the capital is paid into a lawyer or notary escrow account before the SAS is registered, the payment reference must indicate the future legal name and the statutory capital table (répartition du capital). The bank will verify the purpose against the corporate articles and the influx must be reconciled with the incorporation capital certificate and the French commercial registry KBIS. For investments exceeding EUR 50 million or in sectors subject to sector-specific regulation, additional pre-transaction authorization files may be required, although a typical tabletop gaming accessories SAS does not trigger French foreign-investment screening.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements to EU/EEA suppliers use SEPA Credit Transfer to the beneficiary’s IBAN, with structured remittance information quoting the purchase order and invoice number. For non-EEA trade counterparties (e.g., epoxy resin chemical exporters in Asia, custom mold makers, or polyhedral dice moulding subcontractors), the preferred clearing rails are SWIFT MT103, MT202/MT202COV if a cover payment is required, and documentary letters of credit for high-value raw material consignments. Commercial Letters of Credit are opened at the French bank through the issuance of an irrevocable LC advised to the foreign beneficiary’s bank; the underlying invoice, packing list, bill of lading/airway bill, and certificate of origin become the conformity documents. To avoid FX exposure on the payable side, the SAS may request the money transfer be executed in euros even for non-EEA beneficiaries, or it may purchase forward cover as further described in the hedging section.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward foreign exchange contracts with French/EEA banks for hedging commercial receivables and payables exceeding 12 months of forecast cash flows; available freely for EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/JPY, and any freely convertible currency.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permitted only in very limited cases and generally unavailable because the EUR is fully convertible and an NDF would have no lawful purpose; French banks do not offer NDF contracts for euro conversion against liquid currencies.

Plain-vanilla cross-currency swaps are available for hedging multi-currency loans, trade-finance facilities, or substantial supplier prepayment structures and must be documented under the ISDA Master Agreement with French ACPR-compliant collateral and EMIR margin rules.

Currency options (OTC and exchange-traded) are permissible to hedge foreign-currency auction settlement risk from Kickstarter/direct international sales, but they require a board resolution authorizing the hedging mandate and a quarterly mark-to-market reporting process to the French bank.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual approval of financial statements and deposit of annual accounts (comptes annuels) with the Commercial Court Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders must approve the annual accounts within six months of fiscal year-end; the approved accounts (including statutory auditor's report, if any) must be deposited with the Greffe within one month after approval (C. com. arts. L.232-1, R.232-23).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted deposit is punishable by a fine up to EUR 9,000; the court may order the filing under civil penalties; persistent omission for three consecutive years can lead to administrative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and supporting financial annexes (liasse fiscale, Cerfa 2065 series)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) - Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year fiscal year: file no later than the second business day following 1 May; off-calendar fiscal year: within 60 days of the fiscal year-end (CGI art. 223).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a 10% surcharge (40% after formal demand; 80% for concealed activity) plus monthly late-payment interest of 0.2%; the SIE may issue an ex officio tax assessment and enforce attachment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of accuracy of the registered beneficial-owner (UBO) information, embedded in the annual accounts filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Confirmation occurs at the annual accounts deposit (within one month after shareholder approval); substantive changes in beneficial ownership must be declared to the RCS within 30 days of the triggering transfer (C. mon. fin. art. R.561-5).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False or non-updated UBO data may expose the company and its managers to a criminal fine up to EUR 225,000 and imprisonment; separate administrative fines up to EUR 1,500 may be applied by the registry for unreported changes.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) is compulsory when the SAS exceeds at any fiscal year-end two of the three thresholds: balance sheet total over EUR 4 million, net turnover (excl. VAT) over EUR 8 million, or average headcount over 50 employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général, ANC Regulation No. 2014-03); IFRS is only permitted for consolidated financial statements of listed groups, not for the SAS statutory individual accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no standalone annual UBO return; the SAS must keep the RCS beneficial-owner declaration continuously accurate and file updates within 30 days of any share transfer changing beneficial ownership. At the annual accounts deposit, the SAS confirms that its registered UBO data remains correct; any unresolved discrepancy converts the filing into a compliance deficiency.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members / nominative securities ledger (registre des titres nominatifs)
Share transfer ledger (registre des mouvements de titres)
Decision log / minute book (registre des décisions et procès-verbaux)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - 1,100 per year for a domiciliation/registered-office service provider; nil if the SAS uses its own business premises.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - 7,000 per year when the statutory-audit threshold is met; no mandatory audit cost for a below-threshold SAS.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard rate; 15% reduced rate for SMEs on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit)
